_comment: House copy for the Herald. Each story kind has headlines and bodies; one of each is picked per edition. Placeholders in {braces} come from the news desk. The writing model's settings are in press.json. House style: a small-town paper that reports blocky everyday life with complete seriousness. Never cruel, never gory, suitable for all ages.

headlines: {player} Back on Their Feet After Brief Death
Local Resident Dies, Returns, Declines to Comment
bodies: {player} {cause} this week, according to the official notice. Witnesses say the setback lasted only a moment before {player} reappeared in bed, somewhat lighter in the pockets. Friends describe the mood as philosophical.
In news that surprised nobody who knows them, {player} {cause}. The Herald understands they have since respawned and are said to be retracing their steps with great care and some muttering.
Officials confirmed on Day {day} that {player} {cause}. The incident is being treated as a learning experience. A spokesperson for {player} asked that the matter be left there.

{player} completed {count} trades with villagers this week. Local merchants describe them as a fair customer who drives a hard bargain. One villager was heard to say "hmm" in what sounded like respect.
The village economy owes a debt to {player}, who made {count} trades since the last edition. Emerald prices are being watched closely. The Herald accepts no responsibility for any inflation.
Commerce is alive and well. {player} has struck {count} deals with the village's traders, who are said to be quietly delighted and slightly richer.
The town watch is investigating reports that {player} came out on top in {count} encounters with fellow residents. Everyone involved has since respawned. Talks are said to be ongoing.

When raiders came, {player} answered. The village is safe this week thanks to their efforts, and the villagers have expressed their thanks in the only way they know: by raising their prices slightly less than usual.
A raid on a village was turned back this week by {player}. The Herald understands the attackers left in a hurry, and in fewer numbers than they arrived.
Heroism is alive and well. {player} defended a village from raiders this week, and the bells are still ringing. The village has declared {player} welcome any time.
{player} has worn out {count} tools since the last edition, the {tool} suffering most. Blacksmiths report record demand. The tools themselves were not available for comment.

It has been a hard week for tools in the household of {player}: {count} have been worn through, most often the {tool}. Some say this is the mark of a hard worker. Others say it is the mark of a lot of stone.
The Herald notes, with some respect, that {player} has worn out {count} tools this week. The {tool} saw the most use, and the least retirement.

Friends are worried about {player}, who has not used a bed since the last edition despite {hours} hours on the go. A bed costs three wool and some planks, the Herald points out helpfully.
The Health Desk has received a report about {player}, who has gone {hours} hours without sleeping in a bed. Residents are asked to leave a bed somewhere obvious.
{player} jumped {count} times this week. Nobody is quite sure why. Sports analysts call it "enthusiastic". The ground calls it "a lot".
In sport, {player} recorded {count} jumps since the last edition, a figure that would surely impress any rabbit. The Herald wishes their knees the very best.
Residents near {player} report frequent bouncing. Official figures put it at {count} jumps. No complaints have been filed, but several eyebrows have been raised.
{player} ate {count} slices of cake this week. The Herald does not ask what the occasion was. The Herald is simply happy for {player}.
The Food Desk salutes {player}, who has eaten {count} slices of cake since the last edition. Nutritionists have questions. Bakers do not.
{count} slices of cake were eaten by {player} this week. Whether it was a birthday, a celebration or a Tuesday, the town wishes them many happy returns.
The Herald is pleased to welcome {player}, who arrived in the world since the last edition. Residents are encouraged to say hello, and to keep an eye on their chests until introductions are complete.
A new resident has joined us: {player}. The Herald hopes they find the place to their liking, and reminds them that creepers are not friendly, no matter how they look at you.
Please give a warm welcome to {player}, the newest member of the community. Early reports suggest they are settling in well and have already punched at least one tree.
The Herald is pleased to report a quiet week. No great deeds, no great disasters, and not a single resident blown up that we know of. The editor took the opportunity to tidy the office.
Nothing of note happened this week, and the Herald could not be happier about it. Readers are encouraged to go and do something worth printing.
Our reporters searched high and low for news this week and found only peace and quiet. The Herald will be back next edition, hopefully with something to say.
Every resident remembers their firsts, and this week it was the turn of {player}, who {fact} for the first time. The Herald notes the date for the history books, which we are fairly sure we keep.
It is not every week that the Herald can report a first, but {player} has obliged: they {fact} for the first time. Friends describe the moment as long overdue.
Mark it on the calendar. {player} {fact} for the very first time this week, and the town is, frankly, delighted. More, we are told, is to come.
Residents who thought they knew {player} have been surprised this week. The figures show {amount} {measure}, from someone who had barely tried it before. A new chapter, it seems, has begun.
Nobody saw it coming, least of all the Herald: {player} has taken up a new pursuit, with {amount} {measure} since the last edition. Experts say it is the start of something.
Variety is the spice of life, and {player} has discovered a new flavour: {amount} {measure} this week, against next to none before. The Herald wishes them well in their new venture.
It was a week to remember for {player}, who recorded {amount} {measure}, against a usual {usual}. Whatever has got into them, the town would like some too.
Figures released this week show {player} at {amount} {measure}. Their usual is nearer {usual}. Observers describe the effort as tireless, and the results as plain to see.
{player} has broken their own record: {amount} {measure} since the last edition, when a normal week brings about {usual}. The Herald salutes the dedication.
When {who} asked for help in the Exchange, {player} answered: they {deed}. The bounty has been paid in full, and the gratitude is said to be considerable.
The Exchange board has one fewer notice on it this week, thanks to {player}, who {deed} for {who}. Neighbourliness, the Herald notes, is alive and well.

opinions.headline: Editorial: It Is Time We Talked About Gravel
opinions.body: Every resident has a gravel story. You dig up, it falls down. You dig across, it falls down anyway. The Herald does not ask for much. We ask only that gravel be held to the same standards as every other block, and stay where it is put.

opinions.headline: Opinion: Should Creepers Be Required to Knock?
opinions.body: Other visitors knock. Villagers mumble. Even zombies groan as they approach. The creeper alone arrives in perfect silence, hisses once, and redesigns your front wall. The Herald believes a simple knock would go a long way.

opinions.headline: Letters: A Reader Writes About the Moon
opinions.body: "Sir, I have noticed the moon is square. My mother noticed it, and her mother before her. Nobody else seems bothered. Am I alone?" The Herald replies: you are not alone, but you are outnumbered. We suggest admiring it anyway.

opinions.headline: Editorial: In Praise of the Humble Torch
opinions.body: It asks for a stick and a little coal. It lights the way, keeps the monsters at bay and never complains. This week the Herald raises a glass to the torch, the quiet hero of every mine shaft in the land.

opinions.headline: Opinion: The Case Against Leaving Doors Open
opinions.body: It takes no time at all to close a door, and yet open doors remain the town's greatest source of unexpected guests. The Herald does not wish to name names. The Herald simply notes that zombies cannot open iron ones.

opinions.headline: Advice Column: Ask the Editor
opinions.body: "Dear Editor, a villager keeps staring at me. What should I do?" Answer: Nothing. Villagers stare at everyone. It is how they show they care, or possibly how they decide what to charge you. Either way, smile and keep walking.

opinions.headline: Editorial: Why Do We Keep Building on Lava?
opinions.body: The Herald has lost count of the number of residents who have lost a full set of tools to a single careless step. Lava does not negotiate. Lava does not forgive. Lava, the Herald suggests, is best admired from a distance.

opinions.headline: Opinion: Let Us Be Kinder to Chickens
opinions.body: They lay eggs without being asked. They wander harmlessly. They ask nothing of us but a little seed. And yet chickens remain the town's most overlooked residents. The Herald calls for a week of chicken appreciation.

opinions.headline: Letters: On the Subject of Beds
opinions.body: "Sir, I put my bed in the Nether to save time and it went badly. Should I have been warned?" The Herald replies: you are now warned, as are all our readers. Beds belong in the Overworld, and nowhere else.

opinions.headline: Editorial: A Modest Proposal Regarding Endermen
opinions.body: The Herald asks only this of our tall neighbours: if you must take a block, please take one from somewhere that is not the middle of somebody's house. We have also stopped looking them in the eye, which is helping.

outlooks: Creeper outlook: scattered, with a chance of surprise.
Skeleton activity: moderate. Bring a shield.
Phantom warning in effect for anyone who has not slept.
Zombie traffic heavy after dark. Allow extra time.
Slime levels high in the swamps. Bouncy conditions.
Endermen: calm, provided nobody looks at them.
Spider sightings expected on walls, ceilings and in dreams.
Drowned reported near rivers. Swim with company.
almanac: Sheep regrow their wool by eating grass. Leave them a lawn.
A cat on your chest keeps phantoms away, and keeps you humble.
Creepers are afraid of cats. Ocelots too.
Bees will remember who took their honey. Use a campfire beneath the hive.
Gold tools mine faster than diamond, and break before you finish the sentence.
Beds explode in the Nether and the End. The Herald does not recommend testing this.
Snow golems melt in warm biomes. Pack them a scarf.
Villagers sleep at night. Please stop ringing the bell.
Turtles always return to the beach where they hatched.
A compass always points to the world's spawn, not to where you left your stuff.
Axolotls play dead when hurt. It is very convincing.
Cake must be placed before it can be eaten. Etiquette matters.
Endermen cannot cross water. They also hate being looked at.
Foxes sometimes sleep in the day and steal from chickens at night.
A pumpkin on your head stops endermen getting cross. Fashion is optional.
Lightning can turn a pig into a zombified piglin. Keep pigs indoors in storms.
Iron golems hand poppies to village children.
Parrots dance near a playing jukebox. Most of them are better at it than you.
Dolphins will lead swimmers to treasure, if fed a fish first.
Goats can knock you off a mountain. They know what they did.
